title: Summary and review questions
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 2.

keywords.def: An organized political community governed by a single authority.
The operational arm of the state. It makes, enforces and interprets laws.
The supreme authority of a state inside and outside its borders.
A form of government in which the rulers are chosen by the citizens.

en.text: A state is a political community governed by a government. It has four elements: population, territory, government and sovereignty. Government keeps law and order, provides services and security and makes economic decisions. Forms of government are monarchy, aristocracy, dictatorship and democracy. State and government are not the same.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: A state is a formally established political community governed by a government.
It has four elements: population, territory, government and sovereignty.
A democratic government keeps law and order, protects people, manages the economy and defends the state.
Effective government is needed for peace.

screens.title: Unit summary (continued)
paras: Forms of government: monarchy, aristocracy, dictatorship and democracy.
State and government are not the same.
The state is abstract and permanent. Government is concrete and temporary.
The state includes everyone; government is the people's representatives.

screens.title: Key words of the unit
defs: An organized political community governed by a single authority.
The supreme authority of a state inside and outside its borders.
A form of government in which the rulers are chosen by the citizens.

screens.why: These are the four elements of the state.

screens.text: Which is a form of government, not an element of the state?
screens.why: Monarchy is a form of government. The others are elements of the state.
screens.clue: Elements are the four building blocks of a state.

screens.text: A democratic government holds free and open elections.
screens.why: All true democracies hold free and open elections.

screens.text: A land has people and a government, but no fixed borders and another country controls it. Which elements are missing?
screens.why: No fixed borders means no territory; foreign control means no sovereignty. So it is not a state.
screens.clue: Check each of the four elements in turn.

items.text: A State is a formally established political community that operates under the authority of a government.
The population of a state must be of a single race, religion, language, and culture.
items.why: The people of a state do not have to share these.

items.text: There can be no State without government.
The government, unlike the state, exists indefinitely as long as the state retains sovereignty.
items.why: It is the state that exists indefinitely. Governments come and go.

items.text: Which of the following is NOT a necessary component of the state?
items.why: The four elements are population, territory, government and sovereignty.

items.text: ___ is a form of government in which sovereign power is vested in a group of people considered superior and best qualified to rule.
items.why: That is the book's description of aristocracy.

items.text: Which statement best describes the State?
opts: It is made up of the entire population
It is made up of people's representatives
items.ans: It is made up of the entire population
items.why: The other options describe the government.

items.text: What are the four main functions of government? Tap all four.
items.why: These are the four functions from 2.3.
items.clue: One option is not a government function.

items.text: What happens if one of the elements of the state is missing?
items.why: All four elements are essential. Without one, there is no state.

notes.text: The chapter test draws 20 questions round-robin from the five section tests, rotating ★/★★/★★★, 25 minutes, no clues.
Glossary entries for Dictatorship and Territory are ungrammatical in the book; keyword definitions are rewritten plainly.
